prs.author: Epochex

prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs patch the same `pre_parse_json` exemption check, but they differ in what they actually catch. #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated()` to strip `Annotated[...]` before inspecting the union, explicitly targeting `Annotated[str | None, Field(description=...)]` — the idiomatic way MCP tool parameters carry descriptions. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json()` calls `get_origin()` directly on the field annotation without unwrapping `Annotated` first; `get_origin(Annotated[str | None, ...])` returns `typing.Annotated`, not the union origin, so its `is_union_origin(origin)` check never fires and the function falls through to `return True` (still pre-parses) for that common annotated-optional-string shape — meaning it likely leaves the original bug unfixed for described parameters, the most typical real-world trigger. #2032 does cover a broader set of plain (non-Annotated) simple-type unions (`str | int`, `str | bool`, etc.) that #3056 doesn't address, so that extra coverage is worth folding into #3056 before closing #2032, but #3056 is the safer base to keep given its handling of the Annotated case.

Two distinct technical approaches are represented: (1) suppress/no-op the stream's close() so the stdin/stdout Python objects survive (#2040 "prevent...closing handles", #2722 "closing sys.stdin.buffer/sys.stdout.buffer", #2734 "preserve stdio streams"), vs (2) duplicate the underlying OS file descriptor with os.dup so anyio wraps a dup'd fd instead of the real one (#2737 "use os.dup", #2866 "duplicate stdio fds"). The fd-duplication approach fixes the problem at the descriptor level rather than patching the Python-level close() call, which is more durable against other cleanup paths (GC, __del__, anyio backend teardown) closing the real fd anyway.

Between the two fd-duplication PRs, #2866 implements the same technique in 1 file versus #2737's 3 files — a materially smaller, more focused diff for equivalent robustness. #2866 also matches #2722's file count (1) but uses the sounder descriptor-level fix rather than a close()-suppression wrapper. On smallest-focused-diff grounds within the more robust approach class, #2866 is the strongest candidate to keep.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs patch the same `pre_parse_json` exemption check, but they differ in what they actually catch. #3056 adds `_unwrap_annotated()` to strip `Annotated[...]` before inspecting the union, explicitly targeting `Annotated[str | None, Field(description=...)]` — the idiomatic way MCP tool parameters carry descriptions. #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json()` calls `get_origin()` directly on the field annotation without unwrapping `Annotated` first; `get_origin(Annotated[str | None, ...])` returns `typing.Annotated`, not the union origin, so its `is_union_origin(origin)` check never fires and the function falls through to `return True` (still pre-parses) for that common annotated-optional-string shape — meaning it likely leaves the original bug unfixed for described parameters, the most typical real-world trigger. #2032 does cover a broader set of plain (non-Annotated) simple-type unions (`str | int`, `str | bool`, etc.) that #3056 doesn't address, so that extra coverage is worth folding into #3056 before closing #2032, but #3056 is the safer base to keep given its handling of the Annotated case.
